q: He proposed that acids are any substances that dissociate to produce ____ ($H^+$) when they dissolve in water.
e: He proposed that acids are any substances that dissociate to produce hydrogen ions (H+) when they dissolve in water. Hydrogen ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Strong acids such as hydrochloric acid ____ ionise in water, whereas weak acids such as ethanoic acid only partially ionise.
e: Strong acids such as hydrochloric acid completely ionise in water, whereas weak acids such as ethanoic acid only partially ionise. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Bases are any substances that dissociate to produce ____ ($OH^-$) when they dissolve in water.
e: Bases are any substances that dissociate to produce hydroxide ions (OH-) when they dissolve in water. Hydroxide ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Arrhenius theory has some weak points, one of which is that its application is limited to ____ solutions.
e: Arrhenius theory has some weak points, one of which is that its application is limited to aqueous solutions. Arrhenius acids give H+ in water and Arrhenius bases give OH- in water.

q: It is unable to account for the acidic properties of $CO_2$, $SO_2$, $SO_3$, etc., which do not have ____, and the basic properties of $CaO$, $MgO$, etc., which do not have hydroxyl groups.
e: It is unable to account for the acidic properties of CO2, SO2, SO3, etc., which do not have hydrogen, and the basic properties of CaO, MgO, etc., which do not have hydroxyl groups. Hydrogen here is the element or the proton being transferred in the chemistry of this stem.

q: The Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted (1879-1947) and the English chemist Thomas Martin Lowry (1874-1936) independently proposed a new theory, called the ____ theory.
e: The Danish chemist Johannes Nicolaus Bronsted (1879-1947) and the English chemist Thomas Martin Lowry (1874-1936) independently proposed a new theory, called the Bronsted-Lowry theory. A Bronsted acid donates a proton and a Bronsted base accepts a proton.

q: Acids are ____ and bases are proton acceptors.
e: Acids are proton donors and bases are proton acceptors. Proton donors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids are proton donors and bases are ____.
e: Acids are proton donors and bases are proton acceptors. Proton acceptors is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: An extension of the Bronsted-Lowry definition of acids and bases is the concept of the ____, which consists of either an acid and its conjugate base or a base and its conjugate acid.
e: An extension of the Bronsted-Lowry definition of acids and bases is the concept of the conjugate acid-base pair, which consists of either an acid and its conjugate base or a base and its conjugate acid. A Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: The ____ of a Bronsted-Lowry acid is the species that remains when one proton has been removed from the acid.
e: The conjugate base of a Bronsted-Lowry acid is the species that remains when one proton has been removed from the acid. Conjugate base: a Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: Conversely, a conjugate acid results from the ____ of a proton to a Bronsted-Lowry base.
e: Conversely, a conjugate acid results from the addition of a proton to a Bronsted-Lowry base. A Bronsted-Lowry base accepts a proton.

q: A strong acid has a ____ conjugate base and a strong base has a weak conjugate acid, and vice versa.
e: A strong acid has a weak conjugate base and a strong base has a weak conjugate acid, and vice versa. A conjugate base is what is left after an acid gives away a proton.

q: On the other hand, the $H_2O$ molecule accepts that proton forming $H_3O^+$ ion (____ ion).
e: On the other hand, the H2O molecule accepts that proton forming H3O+ ion (hydronium ion). Hydronium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The Bronsted-Lowry theory fails to explain the reaction between acidic oxides ($CO_2$, $SO_2$, and $SO_3$) and basic oxides ($BaO$, $CaO$, and $Na_2O$) because there is no ____.
e: The Bronsted-Lowry theory fails to explain the reaction between acidic oxides (CO2, SO2, and SO3) and basic oxides (BaO, CaO, and Na2O) because there is no proton transfer. A Bronsted acid donates a proton and a Bronsted base accepts a proton.

q: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can ____, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair.
e: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair. Donate an electron pair: a Lewis acid accepts an electron pair and a Lewis base donates one.

q: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can ____.
e: In 1932, American chemist Gilbert Newton Lewis (1875-1946) proposed that bases are species that can donate an electron pair, and acids are species that can accept an electron pair. Accept an electron pair: a Lewis acid accepts an electron pair and a Lewis base donates one.

q: The $NH_3$ molecule possesses a ____ of electrons (on the N atom) which is shared by the electron-deficient $BF_3$ molecule (on the B atom).
e: The NH3 molecule possesses a lone pair of electrons (on the N atom) which is shared by the electron-deficient BF3 molecule (on the B atom). An electron-deficient molecule does not have enough valence electrons for an octet on the central atom, like BF3.

q: The $NH_3$ molecule, which donates an electron pair, behaves as a ____.
e: The NH3 molecule, which donates an electron pair, behaves as a Lewis base. A Lewis base donates an electron pair.

q: The $BF_3$ molecule, which accepts an electron pair, behaves as a ____.
e: The BF3 molecule, which accepts an electron pair, behaves as a Lewis acid. A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair.

q: Water can also dissociate into hydrogen and hydroxide ions, and the process is known as ____.
e: Water can also dissociate into hydrogen and hydroxide ions, and the process is known as autoionisation. Autoionisation: water autoionises when two H2O molecules make H3O+ and OH-.

q: The number of hydrogen ions that water will receive, determines the ____, which is related to hydrogen ion concentration.
e: The number of hydrogen ions that water will receive, determines the pH, which is related to hydrogen ion concentration. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Although water is a very weak electrolyte and a poor conductor of electricity, it undergoes ____ to a small extent.
e: Although water is a very weak electrolyte and a poor conductor of electricity, it undergoes ionisation to a small extent. Ionisation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In pure water, one $H_2O$ molecule donates a proton and acts as an ____, and another water molecule accepts a proton and acts as a base at the same time.
e: In pure water, one H2O molecule donates a proton and acts as an acid, and another water molecule accepts a proton and acts as a base at the same time. Acid is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Having both proton-accepting (protophilic) and proton-donating (protogenic) properties, water is called an ____ molecule.
e: Having both proton-accepting (protophilic) and proton-donating (protogenic) properties, water is called an amphiprotic molecule. An amphiprotic species can both donate a proton and accept a proton.

q: $K_w$ is called the ____ of water which is the product of the molar concentrations of $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions at a particular temperature.
e: Kw is called the ionic product of water which is the product of the molar concentrations of H+ and OH- ions at a particular temperature. Kw is the ionic product of water, [H+][OH-], and it equals 1.0 x 10^-14 at 25 degrees Celsius.

q: From the measurement of the electrical conductance of pure water, it was found that the concentration of ionised ion was ____.
e: From the measurement of the electrical conductance of pure water, it was found that the concentration of ionised ion was 1.0 x 10-7 mol dm-3. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: In pure water, the concentration of $H^+$ ion is always ____ to the concentration of $OH^-$ ion.
e: In pure water, the concentration of H+ ion is always equal to the concentration of OH- ion. Equal: higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: If the individual concentration of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions in an aqueous solution is equal to $1.0 \times 10^{-7} mol dm^{-3}$ at $25^\circ C$ (298 K), the solution is called a ____ solution.
e: If the individual concentration of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions in an aqueous solution is equal to 1.0 x 10-7 mol dm-3 at 25degreesC (298 K), the solution is called a neutral aqueous solution. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Since the process of autoionisation is ____, the concentrations of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions increase with temperature.
e: Since the process of autoionisation is endothermic, the concentrations of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions increase with temperature. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: In 1909, Soren P. Sorenson (1868-1939), a Danish biochemist proposed the potency of the hydrogen (pH) scale, a scale ranging from 0 to 14 pH that is used to measure the ____ or alkalinity of a solution.
e: In 1909, Soren P. Sorenson (1868-1939), a Danish biochemist proposed the potency of the hydrogen (pH) scale, a scale ranging from 0 to 14 pH that is used to measure the acidity or alkalinity of a solution. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: The ____ to base 10 of the molar concentration of hydrogen ions is used to calculate the pH.
e: The negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of hydrogen ions is used to calculate the pH. Negative logarithm: pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Similarly, pOH is the negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of the ____ ions.
e: Similarly, pOH is the negative logarithm to base 10 of the molar concentration of the hydroxide ions. pOH is the negative log of the hydroxide-ion concentration.

q: At 298 K, the value of $K_w$ is $1.0 \times 10^{-14} mol^2 dm^{-6}$, and so, $pH + pOH = $ ____.
e: At 298 K, the value of Kw is 1.0 x 10-14 mol2 dm-6, and so, pH + pOH = 14. The f subshell holds fourteen electrons after s, p, and d take 2, 6, and 10.

q: Acids have pH values of ____ than 7.
e: Acids have pH values of less than 7. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: For acids, the smaller the pH value (the higher the concentration of $H^+$ ions), the ____ the acid is.
e: For acids, the smaller the pH value (the higher the concentration of H+ ions), the stronger the acid is. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Alkalis have pH values ____ than 7.
e: Alkalis have pH values greater than 7. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: pH values develop their respective different colours with the use of a ____ (in the form of paper or solution).
e: pH values develop their respective different colours with the use of a Universal indicator (in the form of paper or solution). pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: Arrhenius's concept of acids and bases is applicable in the case of ____ of acids and bases.
e: Arrhenius's concept of acids and bases is applicable in the case of ionisation of acids and bases. Arrhenius acids give H+ in water and Arrhenius bases give OH- in water.

q: In an aqueous solution, strong acids and bases are almost completely dissociated (ionised), producing hydrogen ions ($H^+$) and ____ ions.
e: In an aqueous solution, strong acids and bases are almost completely dissociated (ionised), producing hydrogen ions (H+) and hydroxide ions. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: When dealing with aqueous solutions of weak acids or bases, however, more information about the system is required as they undergo ____ dissociation.
e: When dealing with aqueous solutions of weak acids or bases, however, more information about the system is required as they undergo partial dissociation. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: The strengths of acids and bases can be ranked by the ____ to which they ionise in aqueous solutions.
e: The strengths of acids and bases can be ranked by the extent to which they ionise in aqueous solutions. Extent is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Strong acids are strong electrolytes that ____ ionise in water.
e: Strong acids are strong electrolytes that completely ionise in water. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Most of the strong acids are ____ acids.
e: Most of the strong acids are inorganic acids. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that partially ionise only to a ____ extent in water.
e: Weak acids are weak electrolytes that partially ionise only to a limited extent in water. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: The ____ of an acid may be defined as the number of $H^+$ ions that one molecule of acid can produce.
e: The basicity of an acid may be defined as the number of H+ ions that one molecule of acid can produce. Basicity is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called ____ acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Monoprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, ____ acids, or triprotic acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Diprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or ____ acids, respectively.
e: Acids that donate a maximum of one, two, or three protons are called monoprotic acids, diprotic acids, or triprotic acids, respectively. Triprotic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: A base is a substance that reacts with an acid whereas an alkali is a base that is ____ in water.
e: A base is a substance that reacts with an acid whereas an alkali is a base that is soluble in water. Soluble is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Hydroxides of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) and certain ____ metals (Ca, Sr, Ba) are strong bases.
e: Hydroxides of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) and certain alkaline earth metals (Ca, Sr, Ba) are strong bases. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: Like strong acids, strong bases are strong electrolytes that ionise ____ in water.
e: Like strong acids, strong bases are strong electrolytes that ionise completely in water. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: Weak bases, like weak acids, are weak electrolytes that ionise to a very ____ extent in water.
e: Weak bases, like weak acids, are weak electrolytes that ionise to a very limited extent in water. A weak base ionises only a little in water.

q: The ____ of a base is measured by the number of molecules of a monoprotic acid, like HCl, which will neutralise one molecule of the base.
e: The acidity of a base is measured by the number of molecules of a monoprotic acid, like HCl, which will neutralise one molecule of the base. Acidity is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The relative strengths of acids may be determined by measuring the acid ionisation constants, ____, in aqueous solutions.
e: The relative strengths of acids may be determined by measuring the acid ionisation constants, Ka, in aqueous solutions. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The strength of an acid is related to its degree of ionisation, the magnitude of which is reflected by the value of its ____, $K_a$.
e: The strength of an acid is related to its degree of ionisation, the magnitude of which is reflected by the value of its dissociation constant, Ka. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The larger the $K_a$ value of an acid, the greater its dissociation, the higher the concentrations of $H^+$ and the ____ is the acid.
e: The larger the Ka value of an acid, the greater its dissociation, the higher the concentrations of H+ and the stronger is the acid. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The dissociation constant of a weak acid is sometimes expressed on a ____ scale, which for acid is denoted by the relation $pK_a = -\log K_a$.
e: The dissociation constant of a weak acid is sometimes expressed on a logarithmic scale, which for acid is denoted by the relation pKa = - Ka. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: Small $K_a$ values (corresponding to large $pK_a$) indicate ____ acids.
e: Small Ka values (corresponding to large pKa) indicate weak acids. Ka is the acid dissociation constant; a larger Ka means a stronger weak acid.

q: The higher the $K_b$ value of a base, the greater its dissociation and the higher the concentrations of ____ ions will be.
e: The higher the Kb value of a base, the greater its dissociation and the higher the concentrations of OH- ions will be. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: The water is not included in the equilibrium expression as it is in such ____, that the concentration of water does not change significantly with changes in the concentrations of other species.
e: The water is not included in the equilibrium expression as it is in such great excess, that the concentration of water does not change significantly with changes in the concentrations of other species. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: For a base, the dissociation constant is expressed on a logarithmic scale, which is denoted by the relation $pK_b = $ ____.
e: For a base, the dissociation constant is expressed on a logarithmic scale, which is denoted by the relation pKb = -Kb. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: Small $K_b$ values (corresponding to large $pK_b$) indicate ____ bases.
e: Small Kb values (corresponding to large pKb) indicate weak bases. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: When the solutions of an acid and a base are mixed, an acid-base neutralisation reaction occurs, forming ____ and water.
e: When the solutions of an acid and a base are mixed, an acid-base neutralisation reaction occurs, forming salt and water. Salt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Salts are strong electrolytes that completely dissociate into ____ in water.
e: Salts are strong electrolytes that completely dissociate into ions in water. Ions is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Water solutions of normal salts may be acidic, basic, or neutral depending on the ____.
e: Water solutions of normal salts may be acidic, basic, or neutral depending on the salt. Salt is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: The term ____ describes the reaction of an anion or a cation of a salt, or both with water.
e: The term salt hydrolysis describes the reaction of an anion or a cation of a salt, or both with water. Salt hydrolysis is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Salt hydrolysis usually affects the ____ of a solution.
e: Salt hydrolysis usually affects the pH of a solution. pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: The cation $Na^+$ and the anion $Cl^-$ of the salt do not react with ____.
e: The cation Na+ and the anion Cl- of the salt do not react with water. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: The ionic equilibrium of water remains ____.
e: The ionic equilibrium of water remains undisturbed. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Solutions of salts of strong bases and strong acids are therefore ____ (pH=7) because neither ion of such a salt disturbs the equilibrium of water.
e: Solutions of salts of strong bases and strong acids are therefore neutral (pH=7) because neither ion of such a salt disturbs the equilibrium of water. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: The cation $Na^+$ of the salt does not react with water. This is because the product base is so ____ so that no formation of molecule, NaOH, occurs.
e: The cation Na+ of the salt does not react with water. This is because the product base is so strong so that no formation of molecule, NaOH, occurs. Strong is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: On the other hand, the anion $CH_3COO^-$ of the salt is a strong ____ of the weak acid, $CH_3COOH$.
e: On the other hand, the anion CH3COO- of the salt is a strong conjugate base of the weak acid, CH3COOH. A conjugate base is what is left after an acid gives away a proton.

q: The cation $NH_4^+$ of the salt is a strong conjugate acid of the weak base ____.
e: The cation NH4+ of the salt is a strong conjugate acid of the weak base NH4OH. A conjugate acid is what you get when a base picks up a proton.

q: For a salt derived from a weak acid and a weak base, both the cation and the anion ____.
e: For a salt derived from a weak acid and a weak base, both the cation and the anion hydrolyse. Hydrolyse: a weak base ionises only a little in water.

q: If $K_b$ for the anion is greater than $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b > K_a$), then the solution must be ____ because the anion will react with water to a greater extent than the cation.
e: If Kb for the anion is greater than Ka for the cation (Kb > Ka), then the solution must be basic because the anion will react with water to a greater extent than the cation. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: Conversely, if $K_b$ for the anion is smaller than $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b < K_a$), the solution will be ____ because the cation will react with water to a greater extent than the anion.
e: Conversely, if Kb for the anion is smaller than Ka for the cation (Kb < Ka), the solution will be acidic because the cation will react with water to a greater extent than the anion. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: If $K_b$ for the anion is approximately equal to $K_a$ for the cation ($K_b \approx K_a$), the solution will be nearly ____ because the anion produces $OH^-$ ions just as the cation produces $H^+$ ions.
e: If Kb for the anion is approximately equal to Ka for the cation (KbKa), the solution will be nearly neutral because the anion produces OH- ions just as the cation produces H+ ions. Kb is the base dissociation constant; a larger Kb means a stronger weak base.

q: The pH in the human body varies greatly from one fluid to another; for example, the pH of blood is about ____, whereas the gastric juice in a stomach has a pH of about 1.5.
e: The pH in the human body varies greatly from one fluid to another; for example, the pH of blood is about 7. 7.4: pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: The pH in the human body varies greatly from one fluid to another; for example, the pH of blood is about 7.4, whereas the gastric juice in a stomach has a pH of about ____.
e: The pH in the human body varies greatly from one fluid to another; for example, the pH of blood is about 7. 1.5: pH is the negative log of the hydrogen-ion concentration, so a lower pH means more acidic.

q: A buffer solution is a solution that ____ changes in pH as a result of dilution or small addition of acids or bases.
e: A buffer solution is a solution that resists changes in pH as a result of dilution or small addition of acids or bases. A buffer is a weak acid and its conjugate base, or a weak base and its conjugate acid, and it resists pH change.

q: A buffer solution is a solution that resists changes in pH as a result of ____ or small addition of acids or bases.
e: A buffer solution is a solution that resists changes in pH as a result of dilution or small addition of acids or bases. Dilution: a buffer is a weak acid and its conjugate base, or a weak base and its conjugate acid, and it resists pH change.

q: The two common kinds of buffer solutions are solutions containing (1) a weak acid and its salt (conjugate base), and (2) a weak base and its salt (____).
e: The two common kinds of buffer solutions are solutions containing (1) a weak acid and its salt (conjugate base), and (2) a weak base and its salt (conjugate acid). A conjugate base is what is left after an acid gives away a proton.

q: A typical buffer solution for acidic values of pH (e.g., 4-7) contains a weak acid and its ____.
e: A typical buffer solution for acidic values of pH (e.g., 4-7) contains a weak acid and its salt. A weak acid ionises only partly in water, so most of its molecules stay undissociated.

q: A mixture of ethanoic acid and ____ is commonly used.
e: A mixture of ethanoic acid and sodium ethanoate is commonly used. Sodium ethanoate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Sodium ethanoate, a strong electrolyte, dissociates completely in water and provides a large reserve of ____ ions.
e: Sodium ethanoate, a strong electrolyte, dissociates completely in water and provides a large reserve of ethanoate ions. Ethanoate is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ethanoic acid provides a large potential reserve of ____ ions.
e: Ethanoic acid provides a large potential reserve of H+ ions. H+ is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If a small amount of strong acid like HCl is added to this buffer solution, $H^+$ ions from the strong acid react with the base $CH_3COO^-$ to form undissociated ____.
e: If a small amount of strong acid like HCl is added to this buffer solution, H+ ions from the strong acid react with the base CH3COO- to form undissociated ethanoic acid. Ethanoic acid: a strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: If a small amount of strong base like NaOH is added, the $OH^-$ ions from the strong base react with undissociated ethanoic acid to form $CH_3COO^-$ and undissociated ____.
e: If a small amount of strong base like NaOH is added, the OH- ions from the strong base react with undissociated ethanoic acid to form CH3COO- and undissociated water. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.

q: A buffer solution of pH 7-11 can be prepared with a weak base and its ____.
e: A buffer solution of pH 7-11 can be prepared with a weak base and its salt. A weak base ionises only a little in water.

q: A mixture of ammonium hydroxide (ammonia solution) and ____ is used.
e: A mixture of ammonium hydroxide (ammonia solution) and ammonium chloride is used. Ammonium chloride is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ammonium chloride, a strong electrolyte, dissociates completely in water and provides a large source of ____ ions.
e: Ammonium chloride, a strong electrolyte, dissociates completely in water and provides a large source of ammonium ions. Ammonium is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Ammonium hydroxide provides a large potential source of ____ ions.
e: Ammonium hydroxide provides a large potential source of OH- ions. OH- is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: If a small amount of strong base is added to this buffer solution, $OH^-$ ions from the strong base react with the $NH_4^+$ ions to form ____.
e: If a small amount of strong base is added to this buffer solution, OH- ions from the strong base react with the NH4+ ions to form NH4OH. A strong base ionises completely in water and produces a high [OH-].

q: If a small amount of strong acid is added to this buffer solution, $H^+$ ions from the strong acid react with the $NH_4OH$ to form $NH_4^+$ ions and undissociated ____.
e: If a small amount of strong acid is added to this buffer solution, H+ ions from the strong acid react with the NH4OH to form NH4+ ions and undissociated water. Water is often the solvent, the proton host, or a condensation product, depending on the stem.
